title: Polynomial-Time Computability of the Run-Validity Test
statement: There exist a finite Turing machine $M$ over the binary alphabet and natural numbers $C,c$ such that, on every finite bit string $D$, the machine halts within $C(|D|+1)^c$ steps and outputs the one-bit string whose bit is true exactly when the second component obtained by twice projecting $D$ onto the second component and then onto the first component is nonempty and is either empty or begins with $0$ followed by an empty suffix.
